prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: Clearing age-related protein aggregates from brain and body has no solution at the Main KPI of 500,000,000 people cleared of aggregates, though amyloid-beta is a partial exception that must be stated honestly. Lecanemab and donanemab are approved and do clear brain amyloid in most treated patients (donanemab 76-80 percent, clearance in 6-24 months), but they slow decline by only about five to seven months, carry ARIA in 12.6 and 24 percent of patients with boxed warnings, and are restricted to amyloid-confirmed patients with zero or one ApoE4 allele plus MRI monitoring, so they reach a small fraction of patients and clear one aggregate species only (https://www.eneuro.org/content/13/7/ENEURO.0112-26.2026.full.txt). Other aggregates are unsolved: tau antibodies and antisense (diranersen cut insoluble tau yet missed its Phase 2 endpoint in 2026; posdinemab, zagotenemab, semorinemab abandoned or disappointing) and alpha-synuclein antibodies (prasinezumab) failed on clinical outcomes (https://pharmaphorum.com/news/trial-miss-doesnt-dent-biogens-faith-alzheimers-drug). Systemic amyloid depletion remains first-in-human: CPHPC plus anti-SAP antibody in 15 then 23 patients, and cliramitug (NI006-101, 46 participants) reducing cardiac ATTR surrogates (https://mdedge.com/content/amyloid-depleter/antibody-duo-reduces-systemic-amyloidosis-severity). No open-source aggregate-clearance platform exists; open code covers aggregation-kinetics fitting only (https://www-knowles.ch.cam.ac.uk/software). Honest limit: brain amyloid clearance is a known answer, so amyloid-beta-only tasks need their own prior-art basis; the open work is other aggregate species, body-wide clearance and access.
